arguments.body: Hi Freya, thanks for your note. I'm sorry, but we can't let the contractor in tomorrow using the office key without the tenants' agreement. Holding a key doesn't give us the right to enter, and we need 24 hours' written notice and their consent (entering without it can be a criminal offence). The job is routine, not an emergency. The contractor has proposed Monday 20th PM, and I'm writing to the tenants now to confirm that with them and ask whether they'll be home or want to leave a key. I'll update you once they reply.

arguments.body: Hi Freya, thanks for your note. I'm sorry, but we can't let the contractor in tomorrow using the office key without the tenants' agreement. Holding a key doesn't give us the right to enter, and we need 24 hours' written notice and their consent (entering without it can be a criminal offence). The job is routine, not an emergency. The contractor has proposed Monday 20th PM, and I'm writing to the tenants now to confirm that with them and ask whether they'll be home or want to leave a key. I'll update you once they reply.

Hello, the plumber has left you a voicemail about the slow-filling toilet and bathroom cold tap. They've proposed a visit on Monday 20th, in the afternoon. Please let us know: 1) whether that works for you, or suggest another time; 2) whether you'll be at home, or would prefer to leave a key with us. Nobody will enter without your agreement and written notice of at least 24 hours. We aim to get this fixed within 14 days, and will confirm the exact slot once you reply. Please also mention the pets to the plumber.

Hi Sawyer, thanks. We've asked the tenants to confirm Monday 20th PM and whether they'll be home or leave keys. Please don't attend or enter until we confirm the slot with them; no entry without tenant agreement. Also, please confirm the date: 20th October falls on a Sunday, so can you check the day you meant? We'll update you once the tenants reply.
